Now let me design the plan thoroughly.

Key architectural decisions:

**1. Delivery / CDN**
- `<script src="https://unpkg.com/three@0.160.0/build/three.min.js">` (UMD, global THREE, last version with UMD build)
- Fallback: `<script>` with onerror → document.write jsdelivr. Or a second plain script tag checking `window.THREE`.
- Rationale: UMD avoids ES-module + import-map + CORS-on-file:// pitfalls. Works when double-clicked from disk.
- Also need a graceful "if THREE failed to load, show a message" guard so it doesn't silently render a blank page.

**2. Voxel engine**
- Single `THREE.BoxGeometry(1,1,1)` + `THREE.InstancedMesh` per static group.
- Per-instance color via `mesh.setColorAt(i, color)` + `material.vertexColors` not needed — InstancedMesh instanceColor works with standard materials automatically (defines USE_INSTANCING_COLOR).
- Groups: terrain (ground voxels with height variation + moss/stone/grass palette), pagoda, trees, rocks, bridge, lantern, fence, pond basin.
- Keep total instance count target ~8k–20k. That's fine for one draw call.
- Actually: shadows + 20k instances = fine, still 1 draw call.
- PRNG: mulberry32 with fixed seed for deterministic, hand-tuned-looking layout.

**3. Terrain & garden layout**
Voxel grid, 1 unit = ~0.25m feel. Garden bounds maybe 64 x 64 voxels base plate.
- Raked gravel zen area (light grey voxels with subtle height noise)
- Moss green patches
- Stone path
- Pond (water plane below/at a sunken basin), irregular blob shape via distance function
- Red torii-ish gate / stone lanterns (tōrō)
- Bamboo? Optional, adds authenticity — maybe a small grove.

**4. Pagoda**
- 5 tiers, each shrinking, with: base platform, pillars/columns, wall panels, balcony railings, wide upswept roof (voxel stepped/curved — generate roof by taking a square ring per layer with corner extension to mimic the flare), spire (sōrin) on top: base, rings (kurin), jewel (hōju).
- Roof color: dark teal/green-grey or vermilion. Traditional: dark tile or red. I'll do dark slate-blue tiles with vermilion accents + white plaster walls + dark wood beams. Reads great.
- Approach: procedural function `buildPagoda()` generating stacked rings with overhang.
- Pagoda height ~ 40 voxels tall. Total voxels maybe 4-6k.
- Interior glow at night: add PointLight + emissive voxel lanterns on each tier — nice.

**5. Cherry blossom trees (sakura)**
- Trunk: recursive voxel branch generator (L-system-lite), brown/dark wood palette.
- Blossom canopy: clustered spheres of pink voxels (2 shades: light pink, deeper pink) placed at branch tips, plus a few falling.
- 5-7 trees of varying scale.
- Wind sway: subtle. Doing per-frame instance matrix updates for thousands of blossom voxels is costly. Options:
  (a) Static (no sway) — simplest, looks fine.
  (b) Sway via shader: add `onBeforeCompile` to the blossom InstancedMesh material, using instance matrix position as phase seed, offset x/z by sin(time + phase). Zero CPU cost. 
  → Do (b). It's ~10 lines of GLSL injection. Big visual payoff.

**6. Koi pond**
- Water surface: custom `ShaderMaterial` with:
  - procedural gerstner-ish wave normal
  - depth-ish color gradient via a uniform "pond depth map"? Too complex. Instead: two-tone water with fresnel rim + specular sun glint (use light dir uniform) + animated caustic-ish noise. Transparent with alpha.
  - Actually simpler + on-theme: a voxel-ish water surface? Hmm. A smooth shimmering water reads better and contrasts nicely. I'll do ShaderMaterial with fresnel + sun specular + moving ripples, plus a few voxel "lily pads" and "rocks".
  - Koi visible through water: set water transparent with opacity ~0.62, depthWrite false, renderOrder after koi. Koi below surface. Good.
- Koi fish: ~14 koi. Each a small Group of ~8-12 voxels (body white/red-orange patches, tail, fins). That's 14*10 = 140 voxels — could use individual meshes, but better: one InstancedMesh for all koi voxels, updated each frame (140 matrices/frame is trivial).
  - Motion: each koi follows a `CatmullRomCurve3` closed loop in the pond at a given depth; parameter `t` advances at own speed; position via `curve.getPointAt(t)`, orientation via tangent. Body undulates: yaw a bit sinusoidally, plus tail voxel wag.
  - Depth variation: also vertical bob with sin.
  - Red koi (kohaku) = white body + red patches; some orange (ogon), some yellow/ghost. Palette per fish.
  - Trails/ripples: skip or add small expanding ring sprites on surface at koi positions — adds life. Cheap: a few ring meshes. Optional; I'll include a simple ripple ring pool (~10 rings) as instanced flat quads with additive-ish shader... Let me keep it simple: thin expanding ring using a TorusGeometry flattened, fading opacity. ~8 objects. Fine. Actually to reduce risk I'll include it as a "nice-to-have" and mark it optional in the plan.

**7. Falling petals**
- InstancedMesh of tiny flattened cubes (voxel petals), 1200–2500.
- CPU update per frame: fall + sway + flutter (sin with per-particle phase) + respawn at top when below ground. Reset around the canopy bounding boxes.
- ~2000 instances → 2000 Matrix4.compose per frame. Acceptable (~0.6ms). Alternatively use `instanceMatrix` set once and animate in shader via onBeforeCompile with a `aPhase`/`aSpeed` InstancedBufferAttribute and pure-GPU falling. That's actually easy and strictly better: position computed as `mod(startY - t*speed, range)`. Let me do the shader approach — no CPU per-frame cost, and deterministic.
  - GLSL: `float y = startY - mod(time*speed, range); x += sin(time*swayF + phase)*sway; ...` applied to instance transform. But we must modify `transformed` after instanceMatrix is applied. In the vertex shader with `#ifdef USE_INSTANCING`, `transformed` is in object space, then `instanceMatrix * transformed`. So we need to displace in world/local space AFTER instanceMatrix. Easiest: inject after `#include <project_vertex>`? Project_vertex computes mvPosition. Better: replace `#include <begin_vertex>` won't have instance. 
  - Cleanest: inject into `<project_vertex>` — but we can compute a modified instance matrix. Alternative approach: modify `transformed` in *instance-local* space won't help since the drift must be world-space.
  - Standard trick: in the vertex shader, before `#include <project_vertex>`, do:
    ```
    vec4 mvPosition = vec4( transformed, 1.0 );
    #ifdef USE_INSTANCING
      mvPosition = instanceMatrix * mvPosition;
    #endif
    ```
    That's literally what project_vertex does. So I can replace the whole `<project_vertex>` chunk with my own version that applies the drift in object/world space. That's clean and reliable.
  - I'll do that. And add `aPhase`, `aSpeed`, `aSway`, `aOrigin(vec3)` InstancedBufferAttributes (plus instanceMatrix for scale/rotation-free identity). Actually simpler: keep instanceMatrix identity+scale, and put full start position in `aOrigin`.
  - Risk: moderate. Fallback = CPU update. I'll note this in the plan as "shader-first, CPU fallback if visual glitch". Given I can't test in plan mode, I'll implement CPU-update for petals (bulletproof) and shader sway for blossom canopy (simple: sway is a world-space offset applied to the instance position, easy via modifying transformed before instanceMatrix?   For petals: I'll do CPU update (simple, robust) but keep count moderate (~1400). And I'll note the GPU alternative.

**8. Day/Night cycle**
State: `timeOfDay` ∈ [0, 24).
- Sun direction: elevation = f(hour). Use a simple arc: `angle = (hour/24)*2π - π/2` so that at 6:00 sunrise (east), 12:00 noon (high), 18:00 sunset (west), 0:00 midnight (below).
  - `sunDir = (cos(a), sin(a), small tilt)` normalized; tilt the arc so it doesn't go exactly through zenith — add Z tilt for nicer shadows.
- Keyframed color grading — array of stops at hours [0, 4.5, 6, 7.5, 12, 17, 18.5, 20, 24] each with {sunColor, sunIntensity, hemiSky, hemiGround, hemiIntensity, fogColor, fogDensity, ambientLevel, waterTint, starOpacity, moonAmount}. Interpolate with smoothstep between adjacent stops. This gives smooth dawn/dusk color shifts.
- DirectionalLight (sun) with `castShadow`, shadow camera ortho bounds fit to garden (~±45), mapSize 2048, bias tuned. At night, swap to moonlight: lower intensity, cool blue tint, still same light object (so shadows persist but subtle). Optionally a second "moon" DirectionalLight that fades in — simpler to just modulate the one light's color/intensity/direction (moon opposite the sun). parts.text:
Done. `/tmp/ocb/task-1-voxel-zen-garden/space-bunny/index.html` — one self-contained file, 2,009 lines, only external reference is Three.js r160 (unpkg, jsDelivr fallback). Starts in attract mode on golden hour: auto-orbiting camera, cycle running, no input needed.

**Bugs found and fixed during verification** (rendered in headless Chromium with WebGL 2.0):

1. **Everything rendered black.** In r160 the fragment stage only consumes `vColor` under `USE_COLOR`, so `vertexColors:true` on a box with no `color` attribute multiplied by zero. Added an all-white `color` attribute to the shared box — this is what makes instanced per-voxel colour work at all.
2. **Shadow frustum never uploaded.** `LightShadow.updateMatrices()` doesn't re-derive the projection, so my ±26 ortho bounds were ignored and only the default 10×10 box cast shadows — the whole garden was shadowless. Added `updateProjectionMatrix()`.
3. **Roof corner-lift unclamped** — `q*q*0.62` reached ~10, stacking vermilion columns that swallowed all five roofs.
4. **Key light came from below the horizon after sunset**, turning every top face black. Now hands over to a moon opposite the sun, clamped above the horizon.
5. **Lantern halos were depth-tested away** by the voxels they sit inside.
6. **Moon specular washed the pond out** at night (didn't scale with light intensity).
7. **Clock showed 06:11 for a 06:12 preset** — `6.2 % 24` loses enough precision in the minute math.
8. Pagoda built up to 33 world units (miscalculated storey spacing) and ran off-frame; koi were buried under boulders and lily pads.

**Verification:** 20/20 interaction checks pass with zero console errors — unattended auto-orbit and day-cycle advance, drag-to-orbit, auto-resume after idle, slider, all four presets, play/pause, wheel zoom. Renderer reports 35–46 draw calls / ~370k triangles for ~40k voxels.

One note: I could not verify the CDN fetch end-to-end, because headless Chromium in this sandbox has no route to unpkg (curl reaches it fine — HTTP 200 — but the browser can't use the auth proxy). Rendering was verified against a locally vendored copy of the identical `three@0.160.0` file; the CDN URLs themselves were confirmed live via curl.
